picks.name: Mt Tabor Monday
picks.description: A free Monday evening of live music in the park — Amber Russell and Nathan Watt set up at Mt. Tabor for an outdoor show.

picks.name: Moth StorySLAM: Schooled
picks.description: True stories, told live and unscripted — The Moth's competitive storytelling night hits the Old Church Concert Hall. Theme: "Schooled." Ten storytellers, five minutes each, audience does the scoring.

picks.name: Pre-Inflation Tuesday
picks.description: Sugar Hill on SE Belmont rolls back prices every Tuesday — Back to when we could afford to go out. $1 oysters, $3 cheeseburgers, $3 fries, $3 beers and shots. Great neighborhood bar, no cover, no fuss.

picks.name: Tuesday Splashdown
picks.description: It's gonna be HOT! Free music and immaculate vibes at Audrey McCall Beach. It's rocky so bring chairs or better yet - floats.

picks.name: OPSFest: Midsommer
picks.description: The Original Practice Shakespeare festival brings an abridged Midsummer Night's Dream to Gateway Discovery Park — free, outdoors, and delightful. Bring a blanket and your best iambic pentameter.

picks.name: Society Hotel Rooftop
picks.description: Free rooftop party at the Society Hotel — live DJs, summer air, and a view of Portland from 6 to 9 PM. One of those spots where the setting does half the work for you.

picks.name: Pick It Up, Portland!
picks.description: SOLVE's citywide cleanup brings Portlanders together to pick up trash around the city — free snacks, drinks, and raffles sweeten the deal. A few hours of good work and the city feels a little lighter.

picks.name: First Thursday
picks.description: The Pearl District's monthly art walk — galleries open late, the neighborhood comes alive with people, and the 20-somethings are all dressed to impress. Free to wander, tons of vendors.

picks.name: Ghosts of Summer
picks.description: "A Summer festival for Halloween Lovers": Ghosts of Summer takes over Redd East Event Space. Tickets from $13, grab them ahead of time.

picks.name: R&B Afterdark Block Party
picks.description: A free outdoor R&B block party at the Depave lot on SE Washington and 7th — live music, a good crowd, and the part of town where you might stumble onto another adventure.

picks.name: Lloyd Center Funeral
picks.description: Portland's iconic 1960s mall — the first in the world with an indoor ice rink — closes its doors for good this weekend. Dress in your best funeral gear (or Tonya Harding outfit) and loop through the parking structures one last time, ending at the rink for a skating exhibition and optional jam skate. Free ride; $20 all-day skate rental.

picks.name: World Naked Bike Ride
picks.description: Portland's annual naked bike ride returns — a joyful, clothing-optional protest against any number of causes. Thousands of riders, start point released day-of. Quintessentially Portland. If you're confused because there was another, similarly named naked bike ride a few weeks ago, there's a whole backstory. DM and we will fill you in as best we can.

picks.name: Elephant Garlic Festival
picks.description: The North Plains Elephant Garlic Festival returns — food, crafts, live entertainment, and the annual gathering of the garlic-loving community. Free, family-friendly, and a genuine Oregon tradition.

picks.name: Wash. Park Summer Fest
picks.description: The Washington Park Summer Festival brings an evening of original soul music featuring Portland legend Ural Thomas and the Pain to the Rose Garden Amphitheater. Free concert under summer skies — one of the great summer nights in the city.
